messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call: large anomalous spike detected on /v1/embeddings (12x baseline, sustained for 6m). Auto-alert: high token rate + qps. Trace sample shows identical User-Agent and no referer. Root TS 1777777777
sam: I'm looking. seeing the same — region: eu-west-1 is hottest, embeddings cluster cpus at 95%. Correlates with far higher batch sizes than normal.
joel: grabbing logs, looks like a handful of API keys are doing very large parallel batch requests with batch_size=512 repeatedly. user-agent "embedding-batcher/1.3" across many IPs.
maria: likely a scraper farm — multiple source proxies. I'd like to hit two live mitigations in parallel: 1) temporary per-key hard quotas (soft -> hard) 2) quick WAF block for the most abusive / repeating ASN ranges. Can we do both?
tia: +1. Also, disable batch endpoint (the server-side batch assembler) temporarily so single small requests are the only path. That will kill the economic efficiency of the scraper.
sam: Agreed. Order of ops: A) apply per-key quota caps B) toggle off batch assemble C) WAF rules D) notify customers/support. Do we have a safe CLI to set per-key caps?
joel: yes. Using internal admin API. Example: 

``` 
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.local/traffic/policy
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
 -d '{"route":"/v1/embeddings","policy":{"per_key_max_rps":5,"per_key_burst":10,"duration_s":3600}}'
```
I'll run that now for the top 50 keys by qps.
maria: I'm drafting the WAF rule. Blocking: top offending /24s and ASN list. Rule will be additive and evaluated at edge. Plan: block and monitor for collateral. WAF change id: waf-2026-03-15-01 once applied.
security-bot: Note: pre-check for customer-owned ASN exceptions. If any of the flagged IPs map to enterprise customers, we should add allowlists.
sam: Good catch — joel, cross-check the top keys against enterprise allowlist.
joel: cross-checked. No enterprise keys in the top 50. proceeding.
joel: Executed per-key caps for top 50 keys. Response: 200 OK. Estimated immediate reduction in request admission ~38%.
tia: Patching feature flag: disable batch-assembler feature. CLI: 

```
redwoodctl featureflags set embeddings_batch false --env prod
```
Done. Batch endpoints returning 403 now for batch requests.
maria: WAF rule applied (waf-2026-03-15-01). Blocking ~120 unique IPs and several ASN blocks. Edge logs show blocked traffic increasing.
incident-bot: Mitigation summary: per-key caps enforced, batch assembler disabled, WAF blocks applied. Observed effect: ingress qps down 64% in 5 minutes; embeddings cluster cpu -> 62% from 95%.
sam: Nice work. Any customer-facing impact? Support, are we seeing legitimate customer errors?
support: We have ~18 support tickets in last 10m referencing 429s on embeddings. Most are small clients hitting expected rate limits — likely part of the mitigation. Two customers (enterprise) reported degradation but keys are not in blocked list. Investigating.
anya: I'll take the on-call handoff in 15m. Current status: mitigations active, traffic stabilized but still > baseline. Recommend keeping per-key caps for 60m and WAF rules for 120m while we observe.
joel: quick safety: enable a canary allow rule for 3 enterprise keys to ensure they don't hit any retry storms. Applied.
security-bot: Note: we should capture packet-level headers for the blocked IPs for later attribution. Spinning a capture on edge-proxy for 30m.
sam: Can we reduce customer noise? Suggest message to status page: "Underway: targeted traffic controls on embeddings due to abusive activity; some customers may see elevated 429s. We're actively mitigating." Drafted message ready.
support: Sending banner now and triage email to SEs. Also posting suggested customer guidance: retry-backoff and smaller batch sizes.
maria: Initial forensics: fingerprint shows reuse of a 3rd-party open-source embedding client with default concurrency; they discovered a bug that makes it amplify parallelism across proxies. We'll add a rule to specifically cap that UA as fallback.
tia: After 20m of mitigations, we should re-enable a reduced version of batch with batch_size <= 8 and strict per-key rps to allow legit batched customers to work. Plan: rollback step at T+30 if stable.
joel: Observed side-effect: two latency-sensitive customers experienced 500s during WAF deployment (edge rule mismatch). Rolled back one IP block to exception and latency recovered. Marking as action item to pre-run exception checks next time.
incident-bot: Metrics update at 1777777830: qps down 70%, tail p95 latency for embeddings back to 220ms, errors (500/429) tripled for small keys but overall successful responses increased.
sam: Good. Let's schedule a postmortem and the follow-ups: - tighter integration between allowlist and abuse detector - automated preflight for WAF changes - telemetry to detect UA-based amplification - runbook addition for batch disable and safe rollback
anya: Handing off active watch to me at 1777777860. I will keep watchers for 60m and escalate if qps climbs by >20% over 10m. Contact: anya@redwood.com on call.
joel: leaving notes in the incident doc and uploading the logs: link https://internal.redwood/incident/1777777777/logs (scrubbed).
maria: post-incident action: schedule ASN/actor cleanup, add UA fingerprint rule, and refine per-key token-bucket defaults to avoid heavy batched bursts.
support: all customer-facing comms sent: status page + 2 customer emails to high-volume accounts.
security-bot: Forensics job queued: asg-dump + proxy-captures saved under s3://incidents/1777777777/ for 90 days.
anya: Wrapping up handoff. Current plan: keep per-key caps 1h, WAF 2h, partial-batch allowed at batch_size<=8 if no resurgence. Next update in 30m or immediate if condition changes.
sam: Thanks team. Filing a quick timeline and assigning owners for action items. We'll run full postmortem tomorrow with SRE + Security + Support. :thumbsup:
